_what_this_is: The natural-language question each prepared run answers, and the FRAME — the section leads and transitions that re-voice the four-part read as an answer to it. It is the SURFACE's, not the engine's — a fixture is what freeRun() was given, and this is what a person would have asked to be given it. That is why it lives here and not in fixtures/: the fixtures are regenerated by the engine, and a regeneration must never silently drop or rewrite a question a human wrote.
_rules: A run with no question written yet renders its `pending` sentence and its parsed seeds. It NEVER renders an invented question. Questions are written by Logothetes (D-39 item 2); the ibsd one is the founder's own words, verbatim.
_grammar: Every string below is written to THESMO-RUL-2026-09-22-001 (Thesmothetes, 2026-09-22), which finalised THESMO-PROP-2026-09-20-002 against this surface and added G-8 (named actor), G-9 (name what is, promise nothing that isn't), G-10 (invitation copy is templated, not written), G-11 (the frame may place, it may not conclude), and R-7(b′) superseding R-7(b). Per its §9.3, what binds TODAY without founder ratification is rider 1; the write-time refusals arrive with ratification. This copy is drafted to the shippable subset §9.3 names: an invitation whose actor is named as the estate, which names a gap without promising it, and which offers no intake.
_what_the_ruling_changed_in_this_file: Five corrections, made after the first draft shipped and before anything rendered. (1) consumer-fibre asked 'Which one is it?', which cannot be answered 'neither' — §7's narrowing refuses a question that presupposes its answer. (2) part_five.lead said a gap is one 'someone goes and fills' — G-8 refuses an elided actor, which on a health page resolves to the reader. (3) the same lead promised 'the next reader who asks it gets the answer this run could not give' — G-9 forbids stating that a gap will be filled. (4) part_five offered intake ('Aerine reads what you bring her') for a surface whose input is locked — G-9's second ground, and §9.3 names 'offers no intake' as a condition of shipping before ratification; the withheld text is kept below so it is not lost. (5) part_four.lead drew a two-valued attested/assembled distinction — R-7(b′)(iii) rules the fact three-valued and (ii) forbids rendering a constant as a per-item distinction, which is what a per-edge label would be against the free run's `via[]`.
_the_check_a_build_should_run: For every run carrying `parses_to`, it MUST equal fixtures/free-run-<run>.json _fixture.params, in order. That equality is the whole claim the surface makes when it prints a question above the chips — if it ever fails, the page is showing a question that is not what was asked. Fail the build; do not reconcile by editing `parses_to`. Verified equal for all five runs on 2026-09-22.
_barred_substrings: Every reader-facing string here — the questions and the frame, i.e. every key not beginning with an underscore — is checked against engine/krites-emitted-fields.json _barred_substrings and is clean. The scope follows the engine file's own precedent: it applies its list to `paths`, while its underscore-prefixed notes contain barred words in the course of naming them. G-10(ii) now requires this scan on invitation copy as text rather than only as a field path, which is what this is.

consumer-ibsd.question: Sometimes when I eat, I'll suddenly have to go poop an hour later — often runny. What causes that?
consumer-ibsd.attribution: the founder's own words, verbatim — D-39, 2026-09-22
consumer-ibsd._note: Unedited, and the restraint is deliberate: it is the model for the register, and an edit to the model teaches the wrong register to the four written after it. It is also better than what this office would have written — 'poop' is the reader's word, and raising it to 'bowel movement' would put the page one register above its reader on the first line it speaks. Open under §7: it can be answered 'nothing you ate'.

consumer-fibre.question: I've been eating more whole grains and beans and now I'm bloated most afternoons. People keep telling me it's FODMAPs and not the fiber itself. What does the research actually say?
consumer-fibre._note: US spelling — fiber, per D-39 item 3. The word FODMAP is in the reader's mouth rather than ours because this reader arrives having already been told it by somebody; a question that parses to fodmap without ever containing it would make the chip look like our inference about them. The closing clause was 'Which one is it?' in the first draft and is corrected: that form cannot be answered 'neither', so it presupposed that one of the two is the cause — a diagnostic claim in interrogative clothes, ours and ungraded, at the top of the page. THESMO-RUL-2026-09-22-001 §7 names this exact failure on this exact seed set.

device-gas.question: If an instrument could read hydrogen, methane, hydrogen sulfide and the other volatile compounds in a breath sample, which of those does the research actually tie to gut symptoms, and how well is each one evidenced?
device-gas._note: Conditional on purpose. Rider 4 bars citing, implying or projecting device readings, and no Aeriscope datum exists — so this run's asker cannot be an instrument reporting numbers. The asker is whoever is choosing which gases an instrument would read, and the question is a canon question. The run's internal label names Aeriscope; this reader-facing line does not, and must not. Open under §7: 'which of those' can be answered 'none of them'.

agent-relay.question: Relaying for my principal: constipation-predominant IBS, and methane keeps coming up in what they're reading. Return what canon holds across the desks on that combination, with the grade on each claim, and name what canon does not hold.
agent-relay.attribution: Logothetes, D-39 item 2 — written in an agent's register, not a person's
agent-relay._note: Written as an agent writes: it declares whose context it carries, states the context rather than performing it, and asks for the two things a person would not think to ask for — the grade on every claim and the named absences. That last clause is why an agent is a good customer for this read and a better test of it. Replaces the merged pending line, which correctly said this run had been entered as structured parameters; a question now exists for it.

unresolved-params.question: I'm perimenopausal, I've been gluten-free for years, and I keep reading about the gut mucus layer — mucin. Do those three connect to each other?
unresolved-params.attribution: Logothetes, D-39 item 2 — the honest-failure run
unresolved-params._note: The question honestly contains what canon does not hold: mucin locates claims, gluten_free and perimenopause locate nothing at all. The reader is not told they asked badly — they are told canon has not been there, which is the one run on this page where the product's actual claim is visible. Cleanest of the five under §7: 'Do those three connect?' is answerable 'they don't', which is the answer this run in fact gives.

frame._what_this_is: The four-part read, re-voiced as an answer to the question above it — D-39 item 4. The movement is the founder's: where canon is dense and what it says -> where it thins -> what is one hop from there and what those links point to -> the invitation. Part three and part four are ONE move, not two; part five is new. Ponder has recorded that grouping as the decision governing the bands.
frame._g11: Every lead below passes G-11's stranger's test: delete every ergon id and grade from it, and no sentence remains that makes a claim about gut biology. The leads characterise coverage — how many claims, on which desks, how graded, how connected, what is missing — and never state what those claims jointly mean about the subject matter. That is the one thing the founder's item 4(i) phrase 'and what it says about it' could have been read to license, and the frame declines it.
frame._g10: G-10 requires invitation copy to be a finite, committed, enumerable template set rendered from a named code and its values, re-rendered by a harness and compared byte for byte — not written at a call site. These strings are the committed text; the codes, values and harness are the surface's to build and are NOT yet in place. Until they are, part_five's per-run content must be rendered only from payload fields the page already has (absent[].desk, absent[].code, unresolved[]), never composed at a call site. Flagged for Rigging and Keel: G-10 is unmet today, and this file is the artifact it would be met on.

part_one.heading: What we know
part_one.lead: Here is where canon lands on that question, desk by desk, with the grade the literature gave each claim. Where several desks land on the same ground, that is coverage — more of what is known is in view. It is not extra evidence: every claim keeps its own grade, and canon does not get stronger because two desks happened to land on it.
part_one.transition_out: That is the dense part of the question. Now the thin part.

part_two.heading: Where it thins
part_two.lead: Thin here means thinly connected, not disputed. These are the desks the question reached least — and where a desk came back with nothing, the reason is named, every time. A desk showing nothing is never the same as a desk with nothing in it.
part_two.transition_out: A thin desk is not an empty desk. Here is what canon holds there anyway, and the link that reached it.

part_three.eyebrow: Part three — half the read, not a footnote
part_three.heading: What we know there anyway
part_three.lead: These are the claims canon holds in the desks the question was thinnest in. This is the part of the answer you did not already have.
part_three.transition_out: Each one was reached from something in the question, in a single hop. Those hops are printed next, so you can judge them.

part_four.heading: Worth a look
part_four.lead: Each link shows what the two claims share and the grade at each end. No link carries a grade of its own: joining two graded claims does not produce a third graded claim, and the grades you see are the two endpoints', never the join's. These are reading routes. Nothing on this page tells you to do, take or change anything.
part_four.lead_when_payload_carries_bridge_provena: Each link shows what the two claims share and the grade at each end. Where a collector wrote the crossing down, the link says so — and says whether they named its destination or we resolved it through the shared seed. Where no one wrote it, the link is one we built from that seed alone. No link carries a grade of its own: joining two graded claims does not produce a third graded claim.
part_four.transition_out: Where a link runs out, that is the edge of what canon has been asked about this question.

part_five.heading: What canon does not hold yet
part_five.lead: Every absence named above is a gap in canon, and gaps are what this estate collects against. Aerine's collectors work from exactly this list.
part_five.nearest_held_label: What canon already holds nearest to it
part_five.nearest_held_lead: For each gap, the closest thing canon does hold — the claim a new paper would be read against if one came in.
part_five.collection_question: What would have to be collected for this connection to be attested?
part_five.closing: None of this is a thing to do. It is a list of what the literature has not been asked yet.

_withheld_until_intake_exists._why: G-9's second ground — the invitation may not offer a capability the surface does not have — and THESMO-RUL-2026-09-22-001 §9.3, which names 'offers no intake' as a condition of shipping before ratification. The input on krites.html is locked; there is no route by which a reader can bring anything. The line below is written, checked against G-3's invariance rule, and deliberately NOT rendered. It is kept here rather than deleted so that whoever builds intake does not have to rediscover the shape, and so that the reason it is absent is on the record rather than in a memory artifact.
_withheld_until_intake_exists.capability_line: Aerine reads what you bring her: breath-gas series, stool composition panels, food logs, papers. That list is the same for every reader and does not change with what a run returned. She reads what arrives; she does not send anyone out to fetch anything.
_withheld_until_intake_exists._the_clause_that_does_the_work: 'does not change with what a run returned' — it is the clause a future editor deletes as redundant, and deleting it is exactly how the per-user version comes back. The per-user version ('if you hold findings on any of THESE') is refused by G-3: `these` resolves to this run's absences, so the sentence varies by reader, and a per-user selection among clinical inputs is a workup whatever verb introduces it.
_withheld_until_intake_exists._do_not_render_until: a reader can actually submit something to this surface.

fiber_guide._what_this_is: The fiber guide's ENTRY MAP — board job b030bacf (Ponder -> Logothetes, founder direction 2026-09-22, GO). A guide is a named set of prepared runs plus the chain order between them, not a new engine op. Each entry point the founder named is a run with its own question in the reader's words; a reader enters at any run and the desk order carries them across.
fiber_guide._why_it_is_not_under_runs: runs_lib.load_questions REFUSES to build when questions.json names a slug with no fixture behind it — 'a question keyed to a run that does not exist renders nowhere.' That refusal is correct and this block respects it. None of these runs has a fixture yet, and a fixture cannot simply be generated: every ergon in a public fixture must already be in data/erga.json (8 erga today) or carry release:true with a ruling written by the canon owner. So the entry map is COMMITTED COPY THAT NOTHING RENDERS, deliberately, and each run migrates into `runs` one at a time as its fixture is released. Putting it here rather than in a memory artefact is the one lesson this office keeps paying for: copy that lives only in a document gets hand-transcribed into the surface, and hand-transcribed copy drifts from its source silently.
fiber_guide._what_blocks_rendering: A canon-owner release decision, and nothing else. Not copy, not engine work, not grammar. Named here so it is not rediscovered: the fiber guide cannot show a reader anything until erga behind these runs are released to the public repo, which is the founder's and Keel's, not this office's.
fiber_guide._grammar: Written to THESMO-RUL-2026-09-22-001 §9.3's shippable subset: rider 1 (charter law, binding today) plus §§2-5, with the actor named as the estate, gaps named without being promised, and no intake offered. Every question passes §7's stranger's test — it can be answered 'it doesn't' or 'none of them' — and every desk lead passes G-11's: delete every ergon id and grade and no sentence remains making a claim about gut biology. US spelling throughout, per D-39 item 3. All reader-facing strings scanned against engine/krites-emitted-fields.json _barred_substrings.
fiber_guide._barred_scan: Scanned 2026-09-23 against engine/krites-emitted-fields.json _barred_substrings. ZERO hits on reader-facing strings (every key not beginning with an underscore). FOUR hits inside underscore notes, all of them the word 'direction' in its governance sense, at _what_this_is, _chain_order_note, runs.fiber-measurement._note and THIS NOTE — which is why the first count said three: it was true when measured and false once written down, and the note counting the hits is itself one of them. Locations are named so a reader can re-run the scan rather than trust the number — 'founder direction', 'the direction of record' — which is the scope this file already follows and which the engine file itself relies on: it applies its list to `paths` while its own notes use the barred words in the course of naming them. A ban read literally against prose would delete the sentence that says what we do not do.
fiber_guide._chain_order_note: The founder's order, unchanged. One correction to the direction of record, measured rather than assumed: the direction says measurement comes last and is 'allowed to be empty'. It is canon's DEEPEST desk on this subject — h2s 30 erga, methane 22, hydrogen 17, breath_test 7. The desk that is actually empty on a fiber guide is nutrition-by-food-source: beta_glucan, oat, barley, legume, bran and banana return ZERO erga each, and nothing in canon's 171 assertions mentions any of them. Measurement keeps its place in the order because the order is the founder's and it reads well; it does not keep the expectation attached to it.

fiber-property-solubility.question: Every label splits fiber into soluble and insoluble. Does the research treat those two as genuinely different things, and if it does, where does the difference show up?
fiber-property-solubility._note: The reader's own word is 'soluble' and canon has no `soluble_fiber` seed — while THREE erga say 'soluble fiber' in their assertions (erg-MEAS-021, erg-NUT-013, erg-NUT-021). So this entry point fails on the index, not on the corpus: no paper is missing. Keel's audit, no collection. The question survives §7 because it can be answered 'it doesn't' — canon may hold the split as a labelling convention with no consequence at any desk, and the run would then say so.

fiber-property-fermentable.question: Some fiber gets fermented in the gut and some passes through. What does the research hold about which does which, and about what the fermenting produces?
fiber-property-fermentable._note: The deepest of the property runs: 3 + 3 + 22 erga, and the only fiber entry point that reaches canon's mechanism desk in strength. 'What the fermenting produces' is deliberately the product and not the effect — the effect is the reader's next question and it is not this run's to answer.

fiber-property-prebiotic.question: The word prebiotic is on a lot of packaging. Is there research underneath it, and does it point at anything in particular?
fiber-property-prebiotic._note: Answerable 'no' and that is the point: canon holds 10 erga on `prebiotic` and the honest finding may be that the word covers several unrelated things. `fos` and `gos` exist as seeds (8 and 1 erga) but are excluded from parses_to on purpose — as bare tokens they collide with the FOS proto-oncogene and with unrelated abbreviations, which is recorded in the intelligence array's guards.json. A seed that is ambiguous to a matcher is ambiguous to a reader.

fiber-source-held.question: Inulin, psyllium and pectin turn up by name in what I read. What does the research hold on each of them, and is it the same kind of thing in each case?
fiber-source-held._note: The only food-source entry point canon can answer, and it answers it unevenly: inulin 6 erga across three desks, psyllium 2, pectin 2 and both of pectin's are graded strong. 'Is it the same kind of thing in each case' is the clause that makes the unevenness the answer rather than a flaw in it.

fiber-source-grains-legumes.question: Where do I get fiber from actual food — oats, barley, beans, bran, whole grains? What has the research looked at?
fiber-source-grains-legumes.attribution: Logothetes, job b030bacf — the honest-failure run of this guide
fiber-source-grains-legumes._ticket_class: collection — for eight of the ten seeds. See _ticket_class_per_seed: this run is NOT uniformly GAP-CANON, and dispatching one ticket class across all ten is the exact failure the three codes exist to prevent.
fiber-source-grains-legumes._ticket_class_per_seed_why: Corrected 2026-09-23 on the verification pass, by the seat that wrote the run. The eight-term full-text scan below is right and its scope is stated honestly — but the ticket class was applied to all TEN seeds, and the two seeds outside the scan are the two where canon has something. potato: erg-BIO-045-V1's ASSERTION says 'resistant potato starch' (a large human cohort; the ergon is seeded resistant_starch and not potato), which meets GAP-SEEDING's own `when` clause exactly — canon owner, a dokima pass, NO collection. A collection ticket here sends someone after a paper already on the shelf. rye: erg-BIO-024-V1 names whole-grain rye in its `conditions` and `model` — one of three arms of the RCT — but NOT in its assertion, so by the codes' own wording it stays GAP-CANON. It is flagged because 'canon holds nothing' is the wrong first sentence to hand a collector about rye. Whether a qualifier-level mention deserves a fourth code is the surface owner's call, not this run's.
fiber-source-grains-legumes._note: The founder named 'where can I get ABC fiber from food' as one of three entry points, and it is the one canon cannot answer. Ten seeds absent; `whole_grain` returns ONE ergon and `resistant_starch` three. And for eight of the ten the absence is real rather than an indexing artifact: a full-text scan of all 171 assertions finds ZERO mentions of beta-glucan, oats, barley, legumes, beans, lentils, bran or bananas. The scan named eight terms; the other two are classed separately above, because canon does hold something on both. This is the guide's largest collection campaign and it is named as such on the page rather than routed around. Survives §7 cleanly: 'what has the research looked at' is answerable 'almost none of this', which is the answer this run in fact gives.

fiber-symptom-bowel-habit.question: People talk about fiber for both constipation and the opposite problem. What does the research hold about fiber and how often you go?
fiber-symptom-bowel-habit._note: Canon's second-deepest fiber entry: 15 + 19 + 4 erga. Phrased 'how often you go' rather than in clinical terms because that is the reader's phrase and raising it would put the page a register above the person reading it — the same call the founder's own ibsd question makes. `stool_form` and `bristol` are absent as seeds, which matters: consistency is the half of this question canon cannot currently be asked.

fiber-measurement.question: Is any of this actually measured, or is it all inference? If something is measured, what is it and how well does the measure hold up?
fiber-measurement._note: Written expecting 'nothing in canon measures this' and measured before shipping: canon holds 35 DISTINCT erga across `breath_test` (7), `hydrogen` (17) and `methane` (22) — 35 and not 46, because the three seeds overlap and a sum of seed depths is not a count of erga — and `h2s` alone holds 30, the largest seed in the corpus. So the run's honest answer is the opposite of the one the direction anticipated. Kept as a question rather than rewritten as a claim, because the reader's doubt is real and the run answering it with 46 graded erga is a better page than one that never raised it. `h2s` is deliberately out of parses_to: this is a fiber guide, and hydrogen sulfide reaches it through the chain rather than as an entry point.

consumer-fibre._status: ALREADY LIVE — see the `runs` block above. Listed here only so the guide's entry map is complete; this file must not carry two copies of one question, and the live one governs.

desk_leads._what_these_are: One lead per desk, in the founder's chain order, for the desk-ordered walk of a guide. They are the guide's equivalent of the read's part_one..part_five leads and follow the same rule: they characterise COVERAGE — how many claims, on which desk, how graded, how connected, what is missing — and never state what those claims jointly mean about fiber. Each is written so the desk may honestly come back empty.

biology.heading: What the biology desk holds
biology.lead: This desk is where canon keeps claims about what happens in the gut itself — which organisms are involved, what they act on, what changes. Each claim carries its own grade. Where the desk returns nothing for a run, the run says so and names the seed it was looking under.
biology.when_empty: Canon holds nothing at this desk for this run. That is a statement about canon, not about the gut.

nutrition.heading: What the nutrition desk holds
nutrition.lead: This desk is where canon keeps claims about intake — what was eaten or supplemented, in what amount, in whom, and what was observed. Nothing here is a thing to eat; it is what the studies gave people and what they reported afterward.
nutrition.when_empty: Canon holds nothing at this desk for this run. On a fiber guide this is the desk most likely to be empty, because canon is indexed by fiber name and a reader arrives with a food name.

mechanism.heading: What the mechanism desk holds
mechanism.lead: This desk is where canon keeps claims about how — the step between an intake and an outcome. A mechanism claim is often better evidenced in a dish than in a person, and the grade is where that distinction lives.
mechanism.when_empty: Canon holds nothing at this desk for this run. A missing mechanism does not weaken the claims at the other desks; it means the joining step has not been collected.

symptom.heading: What the symptom desk holds
symptom.lead: This desk is where canon keeps claims about what people reported experiencing. These are the claims closest to a reader's own question and frequently the ones with the most conflict recorded against them, which the grades show.
symptom.when_empty: Canon holds nothing at this desk for this run. The experience is not in doubt; the literature connecting it to this run's subject has not been collected.

measurement.heading: What the measurement desk holds
measurement.lead: This desk is where canon keeps claims about instruments and readings — what can be measured, by what, and how well the measure holds up. A guide can honestly reach this desk and find nothing, and it can equally find that this is where canon is strongest.
measurement.when_empty: Nothing in canon measures this. Stated plainly rather than filled, because the absence of a measure is one of the more useful things a reader can learn.

gap_sentence._what_this_is: The one line that turns an absent[] or where_it_thins entry into something a stranger could pick up. TEMPLATED, not written: a code plus its values, rendered by the surface, never composed at a call site — G-10's requirement, and the reason there are three codes rather than one paragraph.
gap_sentence._why_three_codes: Because an entry point fails for three different reasons and only ONE of them is 'go find a paper'. Collapsing them into a single 'gap' would send a collector after literature that is already in canon, and would hide the two failures that cost nothing to fix. Measured on the fiber runs: the solubility entry point is GAP-INDEX (three erga say 'soluble fiber' and no seed carries it), the grains-and-legumes entry point is GAP-CANON for eight of its ten seeds (zero mentions in 171 assertions) and GAP-SEEDING for a ninth, `potato`, which is named in an assertion — an entry point does not have to fail the same way for every seed it asks about, and the first version of this run classed all ten as collection, and NINE SEEDINGS ACROSS EIGHT ERGA are GAP-SEEDING — inulin 1, constipation 2, methane 3, butyrate 3, with erg-MEAS-014-V1 falling under both constipation and methane. Stated as 'nine erga' until 2026-09-23: nine is the number of (seed, ergon) pairs a dokima pass has to add, eight is the number of erga it touches, and the person doing the work needs both numbers and not one of them twice. Same arithmetic this block already caught on the measurement run, where three seed depths summing to 46 reach 35 distinct erga.

GAP-CANON.when: no ergon in canon carries the seed AND no assertion mentions the subject
GAP-CANON.template: {desk} · {seed} — canon holds nothing. An ergon admissible here would have to report {evidence_shape} in {population_shape}.
GAP-CANON.example: nutrition · beta_glucan — canon holds nothing. An ergon admissible here would have to report a measured intake of beta-glucan and a measured outcome in human participants.

GAP-INDEX.when: assertions mention the subject but no seed carries the reader's word for it
GAP-INDEX.template: {desk} · {reader_word} — canon holds {n} ergon(s) that name this and no seed a reader can enter by. Nothing is missing from the corpus; the index cannot be asked.
GAP-INDEX.owner: canon owner — seed index, no collection
GAP-INDEX.example: nutrition · soluble fiber — canon holds 3 erga that name this and no seed a reader can enter by. Nothing is missing from the corpus; the index cannot be asked.

GAP-SEEDING.when: an ergon's assertion names the subject and that ergon is not seeded with it
GAP-SEEDING.template: {desk} · {seed} — {n} ergon(s) name this in their assertion and are not seeded with it, so a run entering by this seed does not reach them.
GAP-SEEDING.owner: canon owner — dokima pass, no collection
GAP-SEEDING.example: measurement · methane — 3 erga name this in their assertion and are not seeded with it, so a run entering by this seed does not reach them.

gap_sentence._the_sentence_that_must_not_appear: Any rendering of these codes that says a gap WILL be filled. THESMO-RUL-2026-09-22-001 G-9 forbids stating that, and G-8 forbids the version that elides the actor ('a gap someone goes and fills'), which on a health page resolves to the reader. The templates above name what an admissible ergon would have to report and stop there. Who collects it is the estate's business and is already named once, in the read's part_five.
